subject: GPU headroom erosion — MonetaBank impact summary & executive request
messages:
From: Jill Ramos <jill.ramos@moneta-payments.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.inference.com
Cc: ops@moneta-payments.com
Date: Fri, 01 Jun 2028 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden latency & 5xx spikes in production (MonetaBank)

Olga / Redwood team,

Over the last 90 minutes our production traffic to the reserved model endpoint (curie-512-dedicated) has seen a steep tail-latency increase and intermittent 5xx errors. Impact: elevated response latencies for end-of-day reconciliation jobs (batch windows now extend beyond SLA), and a handful of customer-facing auth flows are timing out.

High-level observations from our side:
- 95th/99th percentile latencies spiked from ~120ms to ~1.2–1.8s over the last hour.
- Error rate climbed to ~0.6% 5xx (normally ~0.02%).
- This endpoint is on your Reserved plan (commit RDW-8321).

We need an immediate sense of whether this is on Moneta's side or a Redwood capacity/config issue. Can you confirm if any maintenance, redeploys, or routing changes were active? We have a large payroll run starting in 30 minutes — this is now a production-risk event for us.

Attachments: sample failed request IDs (stub), short latency export.

Please escalate — Jill
Jill Ramos
Senior SRE, Moneta Payments
From: olga.petrov@redwood.inference.com <olga.petrov@redwood.inference.com>
To: Jill Ramos <jill.ramos@moneta-payments.com>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.inference.com, dylan.brooks@redwood.inference.com, marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com
Date: Fri, 01 Jun 2028 09:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden latency & 5xx spikes in production (MonetaBank)

Jill — thanks for the heads up and terribly sorry for the disruption. I'm escalating immediately and looped in our on-call infra and capacity leads.

Quick transparency: no scheduled infra maintenance from Redwood in the last 24 hours for Moneta's reserved pool. We're treating this as a potential headroom / scheduling anomaly at the dedicated-GPU layer.

Immediate asks (we'll follow up with a timeline):
- Rishi/dylan: start triage & surface any recent config changes, autoscaler behavior, and pool metrics.
- Dylan: export recent scheduling/queue logs and the reserved pool utilization graph.
- Rishi: confirm whether routing policies sent any traffic to lower-tier pools.

I'll keep Jill and Moneta updated every 30 minutes.

— Olga
Olga Petrov
Senior Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
From: rishi.malhotra@redwood.inference.com <rishi.malhotra@redwood.inference.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.inference.com, dylan.brooks@redwood.inference.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com
Date: Fri, 01 Jun 2028 11:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden latency & 5xx spikes in production (MonetaBank) — initial triage

Quick summary of what I can see from triage (first 2 hours):
- Reserved pool for Moneta (pool-moneta-rsvd) shows sustained CPU/GPU utilization at 98–100% across 3 nodes; headroom is effectively zero.
- We observed significant request queuing at the runtime ingress layer — token scheduling latency dominates the added tail.
- There are intermittent CUDA OOM / transient failure bursts correlated with model evictions on one host (node-42). These produce 5xx errors until requests failover.
- Autoscaler: configured with modest burst policy; it did not procure burst capacity — logs show throttling due to a placement constraint (node group quota).

Probable causes (hypothesis):
1) A sudden traffic spike from a Moneta batch + some background rehousing of other customers onto the same rack increased contention.
2) A placement/affinity regression that prevented quick burst nodes from being used.

Mitigation plan (steps we can execute in parallel):
- Immediate (10–30m): route new Moneta requests to an isolated hosted pool variant (hosted-curie-512-econ) while preserving auth keys; this reduces tail latency risk but increases cost.
- Short (30–120m): evict non-critical tenants from the reserved nodes, restart the affected node-42, and drain queued work.
- Medium (2–6h): temporarily increase Moneta's reserved capacity by adding one GPU node to pool-moneta-rsvd (manual commit); we can convert to a short-term add-on charge.

Need approvals on the routing switch (to hosted) and the short-term capacity add. Olga — can you coordinate? I'll prepare the technical runbook and action checklist.

— Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Serving Infrastructure, Redwood Inference
From: dylan.brooks@redwood.inference.com <dylan.brooks@redwood.inference.com>
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.inference.com, olga.petrov@redwood.inference.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com
Date: Sat, 02 Jun 2028 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden latency & 5xx spikes in production (MonetaBank) — ops actions

Executed the following (logs attached and runbook updated):
- Evicted two low-priority tenants from pool-moneta-rsvd (policy: best-effort eviction) — freed ~22% capacity.
- Rebooted node-42 and applied a forced model-resident warmup; observed memory fragmentation clearing on restart.
- Enabled immediate routing rule (temporary) to route 40% of Moneta traffic to hosted-curie-512-econ; 60% remains on reserved pool to preserve throughput behavior for reconciliation jobs.

Preliminary post-change metrics:
- 95th p95 reduced to ~220–300ms on tested paths.
- 5xx rate dropped to 0.08% (still above baseline but stable).

Notes / remaining risks:
- Hosted routing mitigates tail latency but increases per-token cost; finance will need a short-term uplift approval if Moneta agrees.
- The autoscaler placement constraint needs a follow-on patch (INF-2147). If that is not fixed, future bursts will again be manual.

Attachments: mitigation_runbook_v2.pdf (ops checklist), monetabank_slo_graph.png (pre/post graph).

— Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
From: olga.petrov@redwood.inference.com <olga.petrov@redwood.inference.com>
To: Jill Ramos <jill.ramos@moneta-payments.com>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.inference.com, dylan.brooks@redwood.inference.com, marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com
Date: Sun, 03 Jun 2028 17:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden latency & 5xx spikes in production (MonetaBank) — update & exec ask

Jill — short update and an ask for your exec team.

What we did:
- Operations removed low-priority tenants and restarted affected host; we also activated a temporary split-routing to hosted-curie-512-econ for ~40% of traffic.
- Measured improvements: p95 back down to ~250ms for interactive endpoints; 5xx reduced to ~0.05–0.08% and holding.

Why this required escalation:
- Root cause is primarily headroom erosion in the dedicated GPU pool combined with a placement constraint that blocked autoscaler burst capacity. That means this was not a Moneta-only configuration issue — our allocation logic and autoscaler placement need a patch.

Executive ask (decision requested by EOD Monday):
1) Approve a temporary reserved capacity add (1x GPU node) as a billable short-term uplift while we land the autoscaler fix. This mitigates recurrence for your weekend payroll window.
2) Approve routing to hosted pool as a backup pattern for peak windows (we can formalize a traffic-shift runbook).

If Moneta approves, we will: implement the node add within 4 hours of approval, update the SLA notice with the routing fallback, and begin the autoscaler placement patch (ETA 7 business days).

I've attached the ops runbook and a before/after graph. Rishi/Dylan will provide a technical postmortem once the autoscaler fix is targeted.

Olga Petrov
Senior Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
